linkedin.hook: DeFi lending risk is an execution problem, not a collateral problem.
linkedin.copy:
Formal verification of the Blend v2 pool architecture establishes a mathematically sound foundation for Stellar Soroban. While audited b-token specifications secure deposits and interest rate curves, pooled liquidity models still face structural limits when borrowers require custom leverage or automated hedging strategies. Wrapping these mechanics into isolated credit primitives is the missing step.

Vanna operates as this execution layer. By utilizing SmartAccount sandboxes, institutional participants isolate positions rather than mixing risk across a monolithic state. Settlements run with fixed 0.00014 XLM transaction overhead and ~320ms Mercury indexer latency, allowing risk engines to track position health against a strict 1.10x Health Factor floor in real time.

Predictable execution latency changes how institutions handle on-chain credit. Rather than overcollateralizing to hedge against network spikes and delayed liquidation passes, deterministic performance on Soroban allows tighter capital efficiency. Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance.

reddit.hook: Deep dive into Blend v2 b-token verification and building Vanna's credit layer on Soroban
reddit.copy:
Blend v2 recently completed formal verification of its pool architecture and b-token implementation on Soroban. For context, b-tokens handle interest accrual, reserve updates, and pool-level accounting via discrete mathematical proofs. This eliminates common reentrancy issues and math discrepancies at the ledger level.

Vanna sits on top of this verified foundation as a composable credit engine. Instead of users depositing collateral into a pooled vault and borrowing blindly against aggregate liquidity, Vanna deploys an isolated SmartAccount sandbox for each strategy.

The mechanics come down to deterministic execution and state isolation.

Position health monitors maintain a strict 1.10x Health Factor floor. If a position drops below this threshold, the liquidation engine unwinds collateral directly against Blend v2 pools.

Latency is where Soroban shines compared to EVM alternatives. By querying state via Mercury indexers, our off-chain keeper network operates at roughly 320ms latency. Combined with fixed 0.00014 XLM gas fees, liquidation transactions reliably clear before oracles drift out of sync.

If you want to test the architecture, our testnet contracts are live. Point your wallet or CLI to test.stellar.vanna.finance, fund a Soroban testnet account, and instantiate a SmartAccount sandbox. You can supply mock collateral, open a margin position against Blend v2 b-tokens, and test liquidation triggers manually.

Disclosure: I am a core engineer building Vanna Protocol.
